### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **23** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/PROTOCOL_MAP.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via expiresAt (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via expiresAt (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/storage-service.mdx`  _(via downloadUrl (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **23** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/PROTOCOL_MAP.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0f605364698a1ee33d1b4ab909f4d8df105adf87` — the merge of head `0b96e61e15d26cf5936a39d5904db5e07bbc9ce5` into base `7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0f605364698a1ee33d1b4ab909f4d8df105adf87 && git checkout 0f605364698a1ee33d1b4ab909f4d8df105adf87
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a 0b96e61e15d26cf5936a39d5904db5e07bbc9ce5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a && git merge --no-ff 0b96e61e15d26cf5936a39d5904db5e07bbc9ce5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d7943dd0dfba6c98afa2200a08983ec85f9849a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d4b428426e24816b8850828de7bf03c8f42744cd`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

**Read, and nothing else:** card #22158 (body and its three comments: claim `6051529167`, os-dev-report `6053181767`, seat ACCEPT `6053217012`); the ruling of record `6051470224` on #8346, verbatim; PR #22193 (body, its one comment `6053160817` — the docs-drift advisory —, the 54-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head: +1690 / −1565); the head's check-runs. The PR head is the brief's head and has not moved. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the gate verdicts are the check-runs' own conclusions, tallied at the end of ③.

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong against the ruling's words.

**Widenings (additive):**

1. `PageSchema.print` — an optional, closed `PagePrintSchema`: `paperSize`, `orientation`, `margins { top, right, bottom, left }` in millimetres, `repeatHeader`, `repeatFooter`, `pageNumbers`, and the page-break hints `repeatTableHeaders`, `avoidBreakInside`. No `.default()` anywhere (one `PagePrint` type, pinned in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`); every `.describe()` names the print-CSS mapping and the consumer (card ②, later ③). **Right.** This is the ruling's own list — "paper size and orientation, margins, header and footer blocks, page numbering, page-break hints, mapped to print CSS (`@page`, repeated table heads, `break-inside`)" — every item present and nothing beyond it (`page-print.test.ts` pins the key set exactly). Declared-equals-enforced holds: `liveness/page.json` carries the declaration as `planned` with `authorWarn` + `authorHint` naming card ② as the carrier (state-counts planned 0 → 11, the generated count being the authority), and the page form omits `print` with a ledger row in `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`. The `aliases` (`paper`, `pdf`, `printLayout`, …) and `guidance` (`header`, `footer`, `template`) are `strictObject` refusal prescriptions for near-miss spellings, not second spellings. **Right.**
2. New `@objectstack/spec/ui` exports: `PagePrintSchema`, `PagePrint`, `PRINTABLE_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES`, `PRINT_REFUSED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES`, `checkPagePrintComposition` — mirrored in `api-surface/ui.json`, `export-origins/ui.json`, `declaration-map/ui.json`, `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` (`ui/PagePrint`), `authorable-surface/ui.json` (+9 rows) and the regenerated `references/ui/page.mdx`. **Right** — one list in the spec is what lets card ② render the same set the lint enforces.
3. New `@objectstack/lint` exports `validatePrintPageBlocks`, `PRINT_PAGE_BLOCK_UNPRINTABLE` and the type `PrintPageBlockFinding`; the gating rule `print-page-block-unprintable` registered in `authoring-rules.ts` on `ALL` commands with `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['page']`; the author-time rule count moves 49 → 50 in the four CLI transcript pages. **Right.**

**Narrowings (each a refusal that did not exist before this head):**

4. Parse-time refusals, `checkPagePrintComposition`, attached by identifier and pinned in `object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts` (+7 fixtures): `print` on `kind: 'slotted' | 'html' | 'jsx' | 'react'`, on `type: 'list'`, on a `full` page with no `regions`; `repeatHeader` / `repeatFooter` with no region of that name. **Right** — a print page must print exactly the blocks it authors or the subset has nothing to judge, and the `list` refusal correctly routes to `interfaceConfig.allowPrinting`. One looseness, not a breach: `PageTypeSchema` at the head also carries `utility` (a floating panel), which the check admits and the `list` refusal text does not name (it names `record`, `home`, `app`). A nit in ③.
5. The printable block subset: 13 printable, 39 refused each with its reason, 4 retired-by-name left to the parse, and the pin that the two lists classify every live vocabulary member exactly once (`page-print.test.ts`). The lint refuses every other type inside a print page at its `type` path with its reason and the printable list as the fix, one `it.each` case per refused type, every printable type in every container position, the ruling's invoice, and nothing on a page without `print` (`validate-print-page-blocks.test.ts`, 49 cases). **Right** as to the ruling's two mandatory refusals — every row-windowing block (`object-grid`, `record:related_list`, `record:history`, `record:activity`, `object-timeline`, `object-tree`) and every screen-laid-out block (`page:sidebar`, `page:header`, `record:chatter`, `record:discussion`, `record:reference_rail`, `object-kanban`, `object-calendar`, `object-gantt`, `object-map`) is refused — and as to the ruling's named body vocabulary (field blocks `record:details` / `record:highlights`, the all-rows table `record:line_items`, `element:text`, `element:image`) all being in. I checked the borderline declarations in `component.zod.ts` at the head: `element:repeater.limit` is an author-set cap with no renderer default and no pagination (printable — right); `record:line_items.limit` is a 500-row renderer cap with "The grid has no pagination" declared (printable — right, with the cap disclosed; a card-② note in ③); `object-metric` and `element:number` declare no windowing or viewport key (printable — right); `record:alert` declares `dismissible` + `dismissKey` (per-viewer localStorage) and `record:path` is a stage control over `statusField` — refusing both by type is conservative, not wrong: the ruling's two reasons do not reach them and an allow list widens additively. A type outside the vocabulary (`object-chart`, a plugin widget, an SDUI layout block) is refused because nothing answers for how it prints. **Right.**
6. `LIST_VIEW_EXPORT_PDF_RETIRED`: `'pdf'` stays refused in `view.exportOptions` formats (bare array and `{ formats }` alike); the sentence "PDF export itself was declined as NOT PLANNED" is gone; the prescription now names the view's `allowPrinting` for printing a list as shown and "a page that declares `print`" for a document; the `os migrate meta --from 16` tail is untouched, so it stacks with open #22142 either way. `view.test.ts` pins the pointer and `not.toMatch(/NOT PLANNED|declined/)`. **Right** — the ruling's sentence to the letter, and Not-taken A (restoring `'pdf'`) is not taken.
7. The retirement of `data/document.zod.ts` whole: `DocumentTemplateSchema`, `DocumentSchema`, `ESignatureConfigSchema` **and `DocumentVersionSchema`**, with every type alias, out of `@objectstack/spec/data` and the root entry. ADR-0087: four `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR[18]` entries (entry files + regenerated `registry.ts`), one D3 semantic entry `document-schemas-retired` (surface, FROM → TO replacement, reason, acceptance criteria, no `conversionIds`), a `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment; generated baselines −4 defs / −30 authorable rows / −2 defaults; `references/data/document.mdx` removed and the data index, nav, `llms.txt` (203 → 202, data 31 → 30), `PROTOCOL_MAP.md`, the strictness ledger (+ counts) and the quick reference (16 of 30 → 15 of 29) brought to match; pin `document-schemas-retirement.test.ts` with a tree-scoped absence walk over the declared radius, anti-vacuity floors, and a lit control (`DocumentSchemaValidationSchema` survives). **Right** for the ruling's three. The fourth is judged in ③ (within the ruling). No tombstone and no D2 conversion is **right**: none of the four is a stack collection member or a metadata type, so a conversion would have no seam that runs (the #15513 precedent); the `ESignatureConfig` deadline-key rows stay in `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` as history.
8. The pinned-sibling question an export removal must answer (AGENTS.md's "does the pinned sibling import what you are removing?"): the dev's census reports zero readers of the family in objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `a58626c88` and at `main` `cef0eee`, in hotcrm `1e88edc`, and in this repo outside `packages/spec`, each against a lit control (55 files name `PageSchema`; 148 name `FieldSchema`; 77 name `defineStack` / `ObjectSchema`); `cloud` is NOT MEASURED and says so. The `Console Pin Gate` was path-filtered to `skipped` on this head, so the census is the evidence, and it is stated with its controls. **Accepted.**

**The Not-taken list, checked against the diff:** no `'pdf'` on list export; no second authoring vocabulary (the running header and footer are page regions); no Word-upload template kind; no batch merge or packaged download; no in-process layout driver. None taken.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22158-print-page-spec.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: minor`; a **BREAKING** section with the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix ("delete the import; author a printable document as a page with a `print` block"), the ADR-0087 disposition marker `adr-0087: registered document-schemas-retired`, and the declaration `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` at a line start in both the changeset and the PR body — the arm the card's contract notes prescribe. `.changeset/pre.json` is absent on `main` and at the head (both 404 when read); `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` are 17.7.0 at the head. Under AGENTS.md's rule — "`yes` takes at least `minor`, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING", with the migration and the disposition in the body — `minor` + BREAKING + migration + marker **matches what the diff publishes**: the `print` declaration and the lint rule are additive, the export removal is the narrowing, and the changeset carries its migration. (The dev's phrase "launch-window convention" is not AGENTS.md's spelling; the rule it invokes is.) `Check Changeset` on the head: success. The `Clause-②` line is **correct**.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and both `open_questions`, each judged against the ruling's own words.

**Open question 2 — the running header and footer as the page's own `header` / `footer` regions (`repeatHeader` / `repeatFooter`), not block arrays under `print`. WITHIN THE RULING.** The ruling's declaration list says "header and footer blocks"; its design sentences say "The template is a page. The body vocabulary is the page's own blocks", "no new visual designer: Studio's page designer is the designer, the print declaration is a few fields on it", and Not-taken B refuses "a second authoring vocabulary beside pages". A block array under `print` would be a second composition root — a new designer surface and a new walk for lint's `walkPageComponents`, the ADR-0087 conversion walker and `walkAddressedPageComponents` (held equal by `page-walk-conversion-parity.test.ts`) — the opposite of "a few fields on it". The header and footer ARE blocks: authored in the page's regions, already walked, designed and placed top and bottom on screen, so sheet and preview agree; the two booleans govern their repetition on every sheet, and `print.header` / `print.footer` are answered by `guidance` naming the region. A print-only letterhead that differs from the screen header would be additive later. No director ruling needed; the seat's A stands.

**Open question 1 — the 13-type allow list against a narrower list. WITHIN THE RULING.** The ruling says "A printable block subset is defined and linted: a block that virtualises rows or lays out responsively is refused inside a print page, with pins" — it prescribes what MUST be refused and leaves the subset to be defined. Every block its two criteria reach is refused (①.5); every body-vocabulary kind it names is in; the additions (`element:definition-list`, `element:divider`, `element:repeater`, `element:number`, `object-metric`, and the three containers) each draw all they declare at any width, by their declarations at the head. Refusing controls, inputs, shell chrome, folding containers and per-viewer banners goes beyond the ruling's two reasons but contradicts nothing in it, and the allow list is the loud form: widening is additive on a named pull, while narrowing later would be breaking. Option B (the ruling's four named kinds plus containers) would refuse `object-metric` and `element:number`, pushing a monthly report's totals onto blocks the subset then refuses — against the ruling's own second-axis sentence (the port customer's monthly report). No director ruling needed; the seat's A stands. First candidates for a named widening pull, for the record: `record:alert` when not `dismissible`, and `object-chart` (outside the vocabulary today).

**Deviation 2 — `DocumentVersionSchema` retires as a fourth export. WITHIN THE RULING.** The ruling's operative criterion is zero-reader under ADR-0049 ("The zero-reader … retire in v18 under ADR-0049 with ADR-0087 entries"); it names the three top-level schemas. `DocumentVersionSchema`'s only carrier was `DocumentSchema.versioning.versions`, so the ruling's own removal makes it a zero-reader export by construction, and ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove then takes it — keeping it would leave exactly the declared-unenforced surface the ruling removes. It is registered the same way (the `data/DocumentVersion` def entry, named in the D3 entry and in the changeset's FROM → TO). Restorable as one entry file and one export if the director reads the ruling narrower; I do not.

**Deviation 4 — the subset rule on the page save door from birth (`CLI_AND_RUNTIME`), while its sibling `validateComponentTypes` is CLI-only. WITHIN THE CARD AND THE RULING.** The card asks for "`os validate` / `os build` and the save door"; the ruling says "the page's blocks are validated at publish today and the declaration adds a few checked fields". The false-refusal budget the sibling waits on is zero here by construction: `PageSchema` is closed and `print` did not exist, so no stored tenant row and no config file can carry it; the judgment is page-local, so the one-page per-write snapshot is its whole input. The dev's save-door probe through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules({ type: 'page' })` and `metadata-protocol`'s runtime-authoring-gate pins cover the wiring; the head's Test Core check-runs are the gate.

**Deviation 1 (H1 falsified) and deviation 3 (structural refusals in the schema, the block walk in lint):** mechanism choices the ruling does not constrain. The parse-time refusals sit beside the two existing `PageSchema` refinements and reach every door; the nested walk reuses the page-block family's shared `walkPageComponents`. **Right.**

**Deviation 5 — about 15 files outside the claim's declared surface** (pins, transcript counts, ledger rows, `llms.txt`, `PROTOCOL_MAP.md`, the strictness ledger, the quick reference, `vitest.repo-tests.json`): each reads in the diff as a gate-forced or kit-forced edit carrying no behaviour. **Accepted.** One cosmetic regression rides along in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`: the untouched `Iso_ui_page__PageTypeSchema` line lost the space after `=` (`=Assert`). Harmless; a one-character fix on the next touch.

**Out-of-scope findings — carriers judged:**
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` still says "PDF export was declined — #1301" (read at the head). The ruling names only the `.ts` sentence, so this PR is within its letter; but it is the same sentence the ruling calls "no longer true", one hop away in a hand-written page. Not blocking. **Recommendation to the seat:** land it as a docs-only follow-up now rather than wait for card ②, which is an objectui card.
- objectui still carries the old "declined as NOT PLANNED" sentence — card ②'s, right.
- "The Studio author's skill learns the print page when ① lands": the ruling sequences it after ①, and `skills/**` is governed and untouched here (0 of 54 paths on the governed register). The seat's governed PR is the carrier — right.
- `docs/NEXT_STEP.md:55` still planning `ui/document-template.zod.ts`: a stale roadmap line, acceptance note — right.
- The page `template` (multi-column) not judged by the subset, and `object-chart` refused: card ②'s call and a named pull — right.

**Nits for the seat (none blocks the verdict):**
- `checkPagePrintComposition` admits `print` on `type: 'utility'` (a floating utility panel) while the `list` refusal text names only `record`, `home` and `app`, and `page-print.test.ts` pins acceptance on those three alone. Either refuse `utility` or name it — a one-line follow-up.
- `record:line_items` prints every line only up to its 500-row renderer cap; card ②'s print rendering should lift the cap under `print` or make the truncation visible on paper.
- Prose counts: the liveness README's "eleven planned rows (the container, its eight keys and the four margins sides)" describes thirteen entries and eleven counted leaves; the PR body's "10 nested keys" is loose the same way. The generated `state-counts/page.md` (planned 11) is the authority; the prose is loose, not wrong.

**Check-runs on the head `d4b428426`** (their conclusions are the gate verdicts; three reads, none waited on): first read 2026-10-08T05:45Z — 36 runs, 20 completed (15 success, 5 skipped), 16 in progress, 0 red; second read 2026-10-08T05:51Z and final read 2026-10-08T05:54Z — 38 runs, 31 completed (26 success, 5 skipped), 7 in progress, 0 red. Skipped: Console Pin Gate and Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), both path-filtered, plus one duplicate skipped instance each of Auto Label and Check PR Size whose sibling run succeeded. Still in progress at the final read: Lint & Repo Gates and Test Core 1/6 – 6/6. This PASS stands on the head's check-runs as read; the seat reads those seven green itself before landing, and a red among them voids this record on this head.

## CI red on `d4b428426`, and it is this PR's. A fix round has been dispatched

`domain:spec` seat 3 (#18883) · session `session_01RPo7FUd6bSnAfkWMAKi848` · 2026-10-08T05:55Z.

- **Failing:** `Test Core (3/6)` → `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` → `src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts:325`. The test "#17501 … control: `page` still serves 24 top-level properties" now reads `expected 25 to be 24`.
- **Why it is this PR's:** adding `PageSchema.print` moves the `page` top-level property count that the `/meta/types` control pins. The dev's local run covered one test file in that package, not the full suite.
- **Done:**
  - Patch round 1 is dispatched to the same dev on the same branch. It reproduces the failure, moves the control to the new count with its reason, runs the full `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite, and sweeps every other test that pins `PageSchema`'s shape.
  - The contract review that had started on `d4b428426` was stopped, because that head will not land. A fresh review runs on the fixed head.
- `needs:contract-review` stays on until then.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b96e61e15d26cf5936a39d5904db5e07bbc9ce5`
